page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.4-64 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with an elevated memory-to-vCPU allocation. The server runs on dedicated Intel Xeon 8358 hardware using the x86_64 instruction set architecture. It is allocated 4 physical processor cores running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, presenting 8 virtual CPUs via two execution threads per physical core. Paired with this compute allocation is 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio that yields 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU or 16.0 GB per physical core.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage or discrete graphics processing units. All persistent file systems, boot volumes, and database stores depend on external block volumes attached across the virtual cloud network. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The absence of local NVMe storage reduces physical hardware dependency and local maintenance overhead, though it introduces operational reliance on network-attached storage throughput for persistent data handling.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the dense RAM footprint makes the instance an efficient deployment platform for systems requiring substantial operational memory without the financial overhead of high vCPU counts. Common enterprise workloads matching this technical envelope include medium-scale relational database engines, in-memory caching solutions, enterprise resource planning services, and business intelligence extract-transform-load routines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.4-64 is a memory-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at 2.6 GHz, the system features 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile yields an expanded 1:8 core-to-memory allocation, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual processor. The instance does not incorporate bundled local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, delegating data persistence to attached block volumes and including one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware favors memory capacity over excessive compute threads, it delivers cost-effective execution for memory-constrained applications. Suitable enterprise workloads include relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers, Java application servers, and transactional data pipelines.
